guide: Claude Code does the repetitive part of editing a talking-head reel (cutting, captioning, checking the frames), and you finish and schedule it yourself. You need Claude Code, ffmpeg, Google Drive, CapCut and Metricool.
1. Record your clips on your phone and put them in a Google Drive folder, or a local folder that syncs to Drive.
1. Install ffmpeg and open Claude Code in a working folder that holds a copy of the clips.
1. Ask Claude Code to transcribe each clip, choose the cleanest take of every line and cut the dead air with ffmpeg.
1. Have it add word-by-word captions and a hook on the first frame, and export a vertical 9:16 file.
1. Ask it to pull still frames at each cut and check that captions and text sit clear of the app's top and bottom interface areas.
1. Save the result to a Drive folder, open it in CapCut for the final polish, and export.
1. Schedule the finished file for Instagram and TikTok in Metricool.
Watch out: Check the stills after every render, because captions that look fine in the editor can sit under the platform's buttons on the phone.

```
You are helping me edit short vertical talking-head videos. I have Claude Code or Codex, ffmpeg installed, a folder of raw 9:16 phone clips at <clips folder>, and CapCut for the final polish.
Build a small, repeatable workflow in this folder that does the following for each clip:
1. Transcribe the audio with <transcription tool, e.g. Whisper> and save the transcript with word timestamps.
2. Where I repeat a line, choose the cleanest take and cut silences longer than <pause length> seconds.
3. Burn in word-by-word captions in <font and colour> and put a hook line of <hook text> on the first frame.
4. Export a 1080x1920 MP4 at <frame rate> fps.
5. Extract a still frame at every cut and flag any text that sits in the top or bottom <percentage>% of the frame, where Instagram and TikTok draw their buttons.
Use ffmpeg commands and a short script I can rerun. Do not overwrite my original clips; write outputs to a separate folder. Return the script, the exact commands to run it, and a short list of anything you could not check automatically.
```
